title: An SRAM-Based Multi-Operand Architecture Implementing Multi-Bit Boolean Functions Using in-Memory Periphery Computing
problem: Conventional SRAM designs use same bitlines for read and write, limiting ability to implement complex Boolean operations in-memory. Multi-operand and arbitrary Boolean function support in SRAM peripheral logic requires new architectures.
motivation: In-memory computing reduces data movement energy by performing operations near storage. Extended SRAM with dedicated peripheral computing enables efficient implementation of complex Boolean functions, reducing memory-to-processor communication.
method: Modified 9T SRAM cell with dedicated read lines separating read/write paths. Periphery circuitry implements M-operand N-bit Boolean operations via compute blocks with equality checkers and product lines using DeMorgan's theorem.
key_novelty: SRAM-based in-memory Boolean function acceleration using separated read/write paths and peripheral compute blocks for arbitrary multi-operand multi-bit operations including XOR.
contributions: Modified 9T SRAM with separated read/write bitlines
Equality checker and product line architecture
limitations: TSMC 65nm is older node; no comparison with other in-memory computing approaches; limited to small operation widths; memory overhead of dual-bitline approach not discussed.
primary_theme: SRAM-based in-memory computing for Boolean operations
